source_model: scalar AC pi-line models with individual apparent-power or current limits on parallel members
target_model: same line models with certified redundant member flow-limit constraints removed
model_scope: two-terminal scalar phasor transmission lines sharing both endpoint voltages; fixed complex transformer ratios and shunts allowed
phase_neutral_ground_scope: positive-sequence or scalar; neutral and ground not modeled
preserved_observations: terminal-voltage feasible set and any objective on unchanged variables
retained_constraints: all nonredundant limits; redundancy must hold at both line terminals
decision_scope: generic optimization feasibility; no switching, outage, investment, or contingency decision analyzed
recovery_map: none required because line states remain; only implied constraints are deleted
provenance_map: line identities and parameters retained; no aggregation or provenance map proposed
implementation: Algorithms 1 and 2 in pseudocode; MATPOWER/MIPS timing study; no public code identified in the paper
limitations: pairwise sufficient identification for common-centered scalar voltage ellipsoids or cylinders; does not address arbitrary multiconductor sets, independent states, or asset aggregation
notes: Full text supplied by user; Table I reports redundant limits and OPF timing for Polish and PEGASE cases
